🎫 Entradas y horarios

  • Salinas Grandes — recorrido guiado comunitario · 💲 ≈ ARS 8.000–10.000 p.p. (jul 2026: 10.000; mar 2026: 6.000; nov 2025: 4.000 piletones / 8.000 Ojo del Salar) · baños 500 · solo efectivo · 🕒 de día; salidas continuas a medida que se arman grupos (1 h) — Se paga en el puesto, en efectivo, sin reserva. La tarifa cambia cada temporada: llevá ARS 40.000 en billetes chicos para los tres más baños. No hay cajero ni señal. · 🔗 oficial

💡 Tips

  • Salida 09:00 en punto: a las 10:30 estás en Salinas con cielo limpio; después del mediodía suben nubes y viento y las excursiones de Salta/Jujuy llegan en manada.
  • Nafta: tanque lleno en la YPF de Tilcara (mejor la tarde anterior). En 130 km de RN52 no hay un solo surtidor; la cuesta consume mucho más.
  • Altura: 4.170 m en la cumbre y 3.450 m en el salar. Desayuno liviano, 2 L de agua por persona, caramelos de coca, moverse despacio. Si alguien se siente mal, bajar es el remedio.
  • Sol y viento: la sal refleja como la nieve. Lentes oscuros (sí o sí), gorro, protector 50 y campera cortaviento aunque haga calor en el auto.
  • Efectivo: guía, baños y artesanías solo en pesos y sin señal. No hay cajero desde Tilcara.
  • En el salar caminá por donde pisa el guía: hay zonas blandas y piletas. Con lluvia reciente hay 2–5 cm de agua: zapatillas viejas o sandalias de goma.
  • La Raptor no entra al salar por su cuenta: solo en la caravana marcada por la comunidad, y respetando la huella.
  • Lunes puente: el Pucará de Tilcara está cerrado (abre mar–dom); por eso hoy toca Salinas y mañana Tilcara.

📍 Pucará de Tilcara (sitio arqueológico, UBA) · Tilcara
Cerro del Pucará, 1 km al sur del centro cruzando el puente del ferrocarril, Tilcara (administración: Belgrano 445) · 🕒 mar–dom 09:00–18:30, último ingreso 17:15; lunes cerrado (web UBA, nov 2026; horario rotulado «marzo 2025») · 💲 general ARS 12.000 · residentes argentinos 6.000 · jubilados GRATIS · menores de 12 gratis (web UBA, nov 2026)
Ciudad fortificada preincaica de 900–1.200 años (según la fuente), parcialmente reconstruida, con vista a toda la Quebrada; recorrido autoguiado por senderos señalizados, 1 h–1 h 30, subida suave de 80 m con escalones de piedra. Néstor y Ana: jubilados entran gratis con comprobante (si solo tienen pasaporte, tarifa general). Visita guiada gratuita solo con formulario online que se habilita cada lunes (reservaspucaradetilcara@gmail.com, tel. (0388) 495-5768); con lluvia se suspende. Feriado 8 dic: martes abre normalmente, pero no pude confirmar que el feriado no cambie el horario.

🎫 Entradas y horarios

  • Pucará de Tilcara (UBA) · 💲 general ARS 12.000 · residentes argentinos 6.000 · jubilados gratis · menores de 12 gratis · 🕒 mar–dom 09:00–18:30, último ingreso 17:15; lunes cerrado — Se paga en la boletería del sitio (efectivo seguro; tarjeta a confirmar). Visita guiada gratuita solo con reserva por formulario web que se abre los lunes; sin guía se recorre libre por los senderos señalizados. Lluvia suspende la guiada. · 🔗 oficial
  • Garganta del Diablo (comunidad de Tilcara) · 💲 ≈ ARS 3.000–5.000 p.p. (2025–2026) · efectivo · 🕒 ≈ 09:00–18:00 — Se paga y se firma el registro en la casilla amarilla del estacionamiento. Sin cajero ni señal. La tarifa se actualiza seguido. · 🔗 oficial

💡 Tips

  • Martes 8 feriado (Inmaculada): Tilcara llena de turistas de Salta y Jujuy desde las 11. Pucará a las 09:00 y Garganta antes de las 11:30, almuerzo reservado a las 13:00.
  • Jubilados: entrada gratis al Pucará con comprobante de jubilación; con pasaporte solo, tarifa general ARS 12.000 (igual barata).
  • Pucará: senderos de piedra con escalones y 80 m de desnivel a 2.500 m; calzado cerrado, gorro, agua. A la sombra de los cardones se descansa.
  • Garganta del Diablo: ripio de una mano con horquillas, nada técnico para la Raptor pero despacio y bocina en las curvas ciegas; el que baja cede el paso.
  • Cascada: solo quien esté seguro de pisada (piedras sueltas y cruces de arroyo). Mirador y dique son para todos.
  • Efectivo para las dos entradas comunitarias y para los puestos; en Tilcara hay cajero cerca de la plaza (a confirmar) pero se vacía en feriado: llegá con pesos.
  • Maimará: la Paleta del Pintor luce con sol de tarde (15–17). Si salís de almorzar a las 15:00 cae justo.
  • Siesta: muchos negocios de Tilcara cierran 13:30–17:00 incluso en feriado; la feria de la plaza no.

Día 19 · mié 9 dic · Huacalera → Uquía → Humahuaca → Serranía del Hornocal → Huacalera 🛻 En la Raptor, por cuenta propia · Huacalera · 120 km

Humahuaca queda del lado oeste del río: cruzás el puente, dejás la Raptor en la zona de la terminal/Av. Belgrano (el casco histórico es de calles angostas y empedradas, mejor a pie).
Humahuaca → Mirador de la Serranía del Hornocal (4.350 m)25 km45 minRP73 (ripio) hasta el desvío señalizado de 2 km al mirador · ripio con serrucho, piedra suelta y horquillas en ladera25 km de ripio: los primeros ≈ 15 km anchos y rectos por el altiplano, después cornisa con horquillas de dificultad media; cierre: desvío señalizado de 2 km hasta el estacionamiento. Con lluvia el camino se corta: preguntá el estado en la oficina de turismo de la plaza o en la YPF antes de subir.

Frente a la plaza de Uquía, sobre la RN9 (lado oeste), Uquía · 🕒 a confirmar: suele abrir de mañana (≈ 09:00–12:00) y después de la siesta (≈ 14:00–18:00); la abre un encargado del pueblo · 💲 contribución/entrada chica en efectivo (a confirmar)
Iglesia de 1691 (torre separada, techo de cardón) famosa por la serie de pinturas cuzqueñas de los Ángeles Arcabuceros: arcángeles vestidos de nobles españoles con arcabuces, únicos en el país. 🔭 Mirador de la Serranía del Hornocal (Cerro de los 14 Colores) · Humahuaca
Final de la RP73, 25 km al este de Humahuaca, desvío señalizado de 2 km; estacionamiento, baños y domo de la comunidad · 🕒 ≈ 10:00–18:00 según carteles que citan viajeros; la comunidad pide retirarse antes del anochecer · 💲 ≈ ARS 2.000 p.p. (reseñas jul 2026 y operador sep 2026) · efectivo · menores de 10 gratis
La serranía plegada de 14 colores a 4.761 m, vista desde un balcón a 4.350 m: el punto más alto del viaje después de Lipán. Hay mirador principal junto al estacionamiento (0 esfuerzo) y un sendero que baja a un segundo mirador más cerca del cerro (8 min bajar, 30 min subir: no lo hagan los mayores, el aire es fino). Baños, domo con artesanías y empanadas, puesto sanitario con oxígeno (reseña dic 2025). CONFLICTO DE LUZ: el brief dice ir antes del mediodía; todas las fuentes (todojujuy ene 2025, jujuy.net, reseñas jul 2026) dicen que la mejor luz es de tarde, 14:00–17:00, porque el sol pega de frente; de mañana el cerro queda a contraluz. Lo marco para que decidas.

🎫 Entradas y horarios

  • Mirador del Hornocal (comunidad El Hornocal) · 💲 ≈ ARS 2.000 p.p. (jul–sep 2026) · menores de 10 gratis · efectivo · 🕒 ≈ 10:00–18:00; retirarse antes del anochecer — Se paga en efectivo en la barrera del estacionamiento (sin ticket formal). Un segundo cobro de ≈ 1.000 por bajar al mirador cercano (reseña ago 2025). Sin cajero ni señal: llevá pesos desde Humahuaca. · 🔗 oficial
  • Iglesia de Uquía · 💲 contribución / entrada chica en efectivo (a confirmar) · 🕒 mañana y tarde, cierra en la siesta (a confirmar) — No encontré horario oficial 2026: ir a la mañana (09:30) es la apuesta segura; si está cerrada, preguntá en el almacén de la plaza. · 🔗 oficial

💡 Tips

  • Orden del día según la luz (decidís vos): A) Como pide el brief: Uquía 09:30 → Humahuaca 10:15 (Monumento, mercado) → Hornocal 11:00–12:30 (cerro a contraluz) → almuerzo 14:00 en Pachamanka. B) Según las fuentes: Uquía 09:30 → Humahuaca 10:15 → San Francisco Solano 12:00 → almuerzo 12:30 → Hornocal 14:30–16:00 con sol de frente → YPF → hotel 18:00. La B da mejor foto y respeta el almuerzo sentado.
  • Altura: 4.350 m en el mirador, 1.400 m por encima de Humahuaca. Mínimo esfuerzo arriba, 30–45 min y bajar; nada de alcohol en el almuerzo si van a la tarde; agua, coca y abrigo (viento helado aun con sol).
  • Ripio: 4H, 30–40 km/h en la cornisa, lejos del borde en las horquillas; rueda de auxilio y presión de neumáticos revisadas en la YPF. Con lluvia la RP73 se corta: preguntar antes.
  • Frío: aunque en Humahuaca haga 25 °C, arriba hay 5–10 °C con viento. Campera, gorro y guantes en el auto.
  • Efectivo: entrada del Hornocal, iglesia de Uquía, mercado y baños. Cajeros en Humahuaca (plaza), pero no cuentes con que tengan billetes.
  • Miércoles: Pachamanka abre (cierra los lunes). El mercado es cosa de la mañana.
  • Al bajar, cargá nafta en la YPF de Humahuaca: Tilcara y Humahuaca son las únicas dos estaciones de la Quebrada.

Lo que sí vale la pena a la tardecita es el Paseo de los Colorados con luz rasante (18:30–19:30). Vuelta de noche 40 km por RN9 asfaltada y tranquila; animales en la ruta.

🍷 Inkillay — wine bar y restaurante de Viñedos Yacoraite · Yacoraite (paraje San José, entre Huacalera y Uquía)
Calle Santiago s/n, Colonia San José (Yacoraite): desvío señalizado desde la RN9 unos 8 km al norte del hotel, luego camino de tierra hasta el viñedo (2.777 m), Yacoraite (paraje San José, entre Huacalera y Uquía) · 🕒 mar–dom 11:00–18:00; almuerzo en dos turnos, 12:30 y 14:30, SOLO con reserva (Perfil sep 2024 / La Nación feb 2024 — verificar que siga igual en 2026) · 💲 menú de pasos a confirmar; vino por copa y tapas
Opción «cerca» para el almuerzo: viñedo orgánico de extrema altura (malbec, cabernet franc, torrontés, riesling) con un edificio de vidrio sobre las viñas y los cerros; menú de 4 pasos de Florencia Rodríguez (El Nuevo Progreso) o copa y picada. Reservar al (0388) 350-8450 unos días antes. Jueves abre. Visita y degustación guiada bajo reserva. Fuente de 2024: confirmá por teléfono que siga operando igual.

💡 Tips

  • Día sin reloj: desayuno tarde, Trópico y capilla antes de las 11 (sol bajo, sombra larga en el reloj de sol), pileta de 12 a 17.
  • Si eligen Inkillay para almorzar, reserven con días de anticipación y confirmen que siga abriendo jueves: la fuente es de 2024.
  • Juella es ripio de 5 km: 20 minutos despacio; no vale la pena si hace mucho calor al mediodía.
  • Purmamarca al atardecer: el Cerro de los Siete Colores queda en sombra (mira al este); el color se ve de mañana. Si van, es por el Paseo de los Colorados y la feria, no por el cerro.
  • Última noche en la Quebrada: tanque lleno (YPF Tilcara o Humahuaca), efectivo contado y valijas listas para salir el viernes 08:30 hacia Salta (≈ 220 km).
  • Altura: 2.650 m en el hotel; después de cuatro noches ya están aclimatados, pero la pileta al sol deshidrata: agua.

🎫 Entradas y horarios

  • Casa de Gobierno de Jujuy – Salón de la Bandera · 💲 gratis · 🕒 lun–vie 08:00–14:00; visitas guiadas en dos turnos (verificar) — Sin reserva para visitantes sueltos; se entra con DNI por San Martín 450. Si quieren la visita guiada completa, se pide por mail a Ceremonial (la fuente de 2023 no da horarios exactos: verificar al llegar). · 🔗 oficial
  • Catedral Basílica de Jujuy · 💲 gratis · 🕒 vie 07:30–12:00 y 17:30–21:00 (fuente 2023, verificar) — Cierra al mediodía: entrar antes de las 12:00. · 🔗 oficial

💡 Tips

  • Orden sugerido en Jujuy: 11:15 Catedral (cierra 12:00) → Casa de Gobierno (hasta 14:00) → vuelta a la plaza → 12:30 Manos Jujeñas (solo efectivo: llevá ARS) → nafta enfrente → 14:30 salida a Salta.
  • Krysys/Krisys Resto (Balcarce 272) cerró definitivamente: no lo busquen.
  • Es viernes hábil: el centro de Jujuy tiene estacionamiento medido y mucho tránsito entre 12:00 y 14:00; dejá la Ranger en una cochera (Lavalle/Belgrano) por 2 horas antes que en la calle.
  • Tramo Jujuy–Salta: 119 km de autopista y ruta de doble mano; radares en Perico y El Carmen, control policial en Cobos. Con el tanque lleno en Jujuy no hace falta parar.
  • Sheraton: la dirección correcta es Coronel Francisco de Uriondo 330 (Marriott y OSM), no 3. Check-in 15:00, cochera ARS 10.000/día. Desde el viernes son 4: Paula se suma (ver día 24).
  • Reservá la cena del viernes a las 20:30 (Doña Salta o El Charrúa no hacen falta; José Balcarce sí).

  • Plan sugerido: 09:00 salida → 09:20–10:30 Quebrada (sendero corto) → 10:45 café en El Castillo → 13:00 almuerzo en Andrés (reservar) → 15:30 Mercado Artesanal → 17:00 Museo Güemes → 18:30 Convento San Bernardo → 21:00 peña.
  • El Castillo de San Lorenzo abre al público mié–lun 11:00–20:00: el sábado está abierto; el martes no (no importa, ese día ya vuelan).
  • Para la peña dejá la Ranger en el hotel: taxi/remís de ida y vuelta (La Casona del Molino está a 4,5 km y cierra 04:00; Balderrama a 2,5 km).
  • Sábado es día fuerte de peñas: reservar Balderrama por teléfono o La Vieja Estación online; La Casona del Molino no reserva, llegar 21:00.
  • Ponchos: mirar precios hoy en el Mercado Artesanal (10:00–20:30, abre domingo y lunes también) y comprar el lunes 14 si querés comparar con Tienda La Fortuna (lun 09–13 y 17–21).
  • Las entradas del Museo Güemes y el posible bono de la Quebrada se pagan en efectivo o tarjeta en el lugar; no hay venta online.

  • Viator 394075P2 – From Salta: Full-day tour to Cachi and Los Cardones National Park (La Quebrada Turismo) · 💲 desde US$ 33 p.p. (Viator, nov 2026); almuerzo NO incluido · 🕒 salida 07:00; búsqueda 07:00–07:45 'dentro de 15 cuadras de la Plaza 9 de Julio'; 10–11 h; máx. 23 pasajeros — Opción A, la más barata (4,4/5, 47 reseñas). Cuesta del Obispo, Piedra del Molino, PN Los Cardones, Valle Encantado, Recta del Tin Tin y 2 horas en Cachi. Cancelación gratis hasta 24 h antes. El Sheraton está a ≈ 12 cuadras de la plaza: confirmar por chat de Viator que lo buscan en el hotel antes de reservar. NO está comprado: solo si quieren. · 🔗 oficial
  • Viator 5674P185 – Cachi and Los Cardones National Park from Salta (Tangol) · 💲 desde US$ 56 p.p. (Viator, nov 2026); 'comida y bebida' figura incluida — confirmar si es almuerzo · 🕒 salida 07:00 (búsqueda 07:00–07:30, hoteles céntricos seleccionados); 12 h; máx. 30 pasajeros — Opción A bis, operador grande (Tangol, 4,4/5, 11 reseñas): Quebrada de Escoipe, Piedra del Molino, Recta del Tin Tin, 3 horas en Cachi con iglesia y museo Pío Pablo Díaz (entrada no incluida). Cancelación gratis 24 h. Confirmar pick-up en el Sheraton. · 🔗 oficial
  • Viator 31845P4 – One Day Tour of Cachi and Calchaquí Valleys from Salta (Nordic Travel) · 💲 desde US$ 35 p.p. (Viator, nov 2026); almuerzo por cuenta propia en Cachi · 🕒 salida 06:30 con búsqueda en hotel; punto de encuentro Buenos Aires 45, Salta; 12 h; máx. 27 pasajeros — Tercera alternativa (4,2/5, 106 reseñas, con más quejas). Entrada al PN Los Cardones no incluida. Solo si las otras dos no tienen lugar. · 🔗 oficial
  • Teleférico San Bernardo · 💲 ARS 25.000 adulto nacional · 18.000 mayores de 65 · 30.000 internacional (ida y vuelta) · 🕒 09:00–19:00 todos los días — Se compra en boletería (tarjeta, efectivo o QR); DNI para la tarifa nacional y de mayores. · 🔗 oficial

💡 Tips

  • Opción B (Cachi en la Ranger): NO. Son 157 km por lado (OSRM 3 h 01; +20 % de montaña ≈ 3 h 35), la Cuesta del Obispo tiene ≈ 20 km de ripio consolidado y sube a 3.348 m en la Piedra del Molino (Wikipedia; el resto, Recta del Tin Tin y Chicoana, está asfaltado — no son 100 km de ripio, pero da igual): 7 h de volante para 2 h en Cachi, rompe la regla de ≤ 2 h desde la base y la de nada de altura. Si quieren verlo, es la opción A (tour).
  • Opción A: reservar con 48 h (hasta el viernes 11) y cancelación gratis 24 h antes; pedir por el chat de Viator que confirmen la búsqueda en el Sheraton (Uriondo 330). Llevar abrigo (a 3.300 m hace frío aun en diciembre), agua, efectivo para el almuerzo en Cachi y protector solar; el almuerzo no está incluido en 394075P2 ni en 31845P4.
  • Opción C (día libre): abiertos el domingo: Teleférico 09–19, MAAM y Museo Güemes 11–19, Mercado Artesanal 10–20:30, Feria de la Balcarce desde 10:00. CERRADOS el domingo: Casa de Hernández/Museo de la Ciudad (lun–vie) y Museo Pajcha, que ya no está en 20 de Febrero 831 sino en la UCASAL (Campo Castañares, lun–vie 10–13 y 15–18, gratis): los dos pasan al lunes 14.
  • RELOJ: hoy a las 16:25 abre el check-in online de AR1491 (SLA 16:25 → AEP 18:30 del martes). Hacerlo para los 4 (Néstor, Ana, Carolina y Paula, reserva UOTFVV) apenas abra; si están en el tour, con el celular desde el minibús.
  • Domingo al mediodía en Salta muchos restaurantes cierran: Doña Salta y El Charrúa abren 11:30; La Casona del Molino 12:00–15:00. José Balcarce cierra domingo.
  • Si eligen el tour, la cena del domingo es tarde (vuelta 19:30–20:00): El Charrúa abre 19:30, Doña Salta 20:00; ambos sin reserva.

🎫 Entradas y horarios

  • AR1491 Salta (SLA) 16:25 → Aeroparque (AEP) 18:30 · Aerolíneas Argentinas · Premium Economy · 💲 ya comprado (LQORRG × 3 + UOTFVV Paula) · 🕒 check-in online abierto desde el dom 13 dic 16:25; presentarse 13:25; cierre de despacho ≈ 15:40 — Cuatro pasajeros, dos reservas distintas: pedir en el mostrador que los asientos queden juntos si el check-in online no lo permitió (Paula tiene 01D). · 🔗 oficial

💡 Tips

  • Reloj del día: 11:15 salir del hotel → 11:30 almuerzo (Doña Salta) → 12:40 pago y salida → 12:50 rumbo al aeropuerto por Av. Tavella → 13:10 entrega de la Ranger / 13:25 en el mostrador → 15:40 cierre de despacho → 16:25 despegue → 18:30 Aeroparque.
  • Entrega de la Ranger a Hernán Esteban: lugar y hora SIN DEFINIR (memoria del 25 oct). Lo más simple: que la retire en el estacionamiento del aeropuerto a las 13:10 (llave, cédula, seguro y foto del tablero con km y tanque lleno). Alternativa: entregarla en el Sheraton a las 12:00 y seguir en taxi (2 taxis para 4 personas con valijas).
  • Si Hernán la retira en la ciudad, pedí 2 taxis o un remís grande desde el hotel hacia el aeropuerto (20 min); Paula, si llega aparte, que vaya directo al aeropuerto.
  • Almuerzo temprano es obligatorio: los restaurantes del centro abren 11:30 y el aeropuerto solo tiene cafetería. José Balcarce abre 12:00 pero es más lento: no conviene hoy.
  • Martes hábil: tránsito normal, no hay feriado; igual salí del centro 12:50 porque la Av. Tavella tiene semáforos y obras frecuentes.
  • Último chequeo antes de despachar: pasaportes/DNI de los 4, recibos de pasaje (LQORRG y UOTFVV), compras frágiles (cerámica) en la valija de mano envueltas en los ponchos.

18. 🎫 Tours and excursions — day by day: how to get there, stops, where to eat and tips

One booked tour, the rest self-drive. The only purchased tour is the Luján de Cuyo wineries day (Trout & Wine, Sun Nov 22, Viator 1459942485, pickup at the Hualta 08:20–09:00). Every other day is done in the Raptor: each card below has the route with partial km and times, the stops (fuel, viewpoints, cafés, restaurants with copyable address and Google/Apple Maps links), tickets and hours, and tips. Rule for tours: Viator only; parks and community gates are paid on site. Research with sources as of Nov 2, 2026 — hours and prices change: confirm by phone the day before when it says so.

🎫 Tickets and opening hours

  • Estacionamiento medido digital (SEM Mendoza) en el centro · 💲 ARS 500 cada 30 min por app (ARS 600 con tarjeta física) · lun-vie 13:00-16:00 ARS 250 en la zona «Siesta Digital» (desde 1 ago 2026) · 🕒 lun-jue 08:00-00:00 · vie-sáb hasta 02:00 · domingos y feriados: no informado (habitualmente libre, verificar en los carteles) — Pay only via the SEM Mendoza app (Android/iOS) or a card sold at kiosks; without it you get a sticker and a fine. Zones: Aristides Villanueva, Juan B. Justo, Belgrano, Sarmiento (Belgrano-Chile), Tiburcio Benegas and around. For the Raptor use the hotel garage rather than the street. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Flight AR1416 lands 16:20: with bags and the Ranger handover, expect to reach the hotel 17:30-18:00. Ask Hernan for the exact handover spot at the airport and that the truck comes with a full tank; otherwise fill up on Acceso Norte before entering downtown.
  • Acequias: Mendoza has open irrigation ditches along the kerbs all over downtown. With a wide pickup, do not hug the kerb when parking or turning.
  • Hotel garage: confirm height and length limits for the Raptor (5.4 m). If it does not fit, ask reception for a nearby open-air private car park.
  • Restaurants open for dinner only at 20:00-20:30 and fill up by 21:30. On a Saturday it is worth booking (Fuente y Fonda and Soberana take reservations).
  • Cash: ATMs along Av. San Martin, but most downtown restaurants and cafes take cards. Carry some cash for the plaza craft fair and tips (10%).
  • Heat: in November Mendoza hits 30-33 C in the afternoon and cools at night; water and a hat for the walk.

Tips not included (10% for the guide is usual). Reconfirm pickup with the operator by WhatsApp on Saturday night. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Sunday in Mendoza: the Central Market and most shops close; few restaurants open at night. The three options above show as open Sunday night on Google, still confirm by phone in the afternoon.
  • The tour lunch is long (2 h) with pairings: no need for a big dinner. A stroll along Sarmiento and Plaza Independencia at 8 pm and something light.
  • Water: you taste 8-12 wines over the day; ask for water at each stop, especially at 30 C.
  • Tomorrow (Monday holiday) you leave 08:30 for the high Andes: fill up tonight if the Raptor is not full (YPF Champagnat 24 h or whatever the GPS shows) and buy the Aconcagua park ticket online tonight (see day 3).
  • Leave the Raptor in the hotel garage: the 2026 sources do not state that street metered parking is free on Sundays.

Day 3 · Mon Nov 23 🎉 · High Andes on RN7: Potrerillos · Uspallata · Puente del Inca · Horcones · Las Cuevas (holiday) 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Mendoza · 374 km

🧭 How to get there

LegkmTimeRoadNotes
Hualta Hotel (Mendoza) → Potrerillos (mirador del embalse)69 km1 h 00Av. San Martín sur → Acceso Sur (RN40) → RN7 oeste por Luján de Cuyo (alternativa panorámica: Av. Champagnat → Corredor del Oeste RP82 por Cacheuta, mismo tiempo) · asfaltoFirst 25 km are urban/suburban (Lujan de Cuyo, speed cameras and traffic lights). Then RN7 enters the Mendoza river canyon and at km 60 the Potrerillos reservoir appears: several pull-offs/viewpoints along the road; the most photogenic is on reaching the dam. Via RP82 (Cacheuta) you go through a tunnel and come out facing the dam. Holiday: leave 08:30 to stay ahead of the local convoys.
Potrerillos → Uspallata (YPF centro, RN7 y RP52)48 km45 minRN7 · asfaltoMountain section with gentle curves and Chilean trucks (RN7 is the corridor to the Cristo Redentor pass): do not rush overtakes. No reliable fuel between Lujan and Uspallata (≈ 100 km): leave with a full tank. Near Uspallata the road crosses the green poplar valley; cumulative from Mendoza 117 km, 1 h 45.
Uspallata → Puente del Inca70 km1 h 00RN7 (km 1150 → 1209) · asfaltoYou climb from 1,900 to 2,720 m past Polvaredas, Punta de Vacas (Gendarmeria checkpoint, sometimes they ask for ID) and Penitentes (ski resort, closed in summer). Strong afternoon wind, 10-15 C colder than Mendoza. Fixed speed cameras around Punta de Vacas / Polvaredas: respect 80 km/h where posted. Cumulative 187 km, 2 h 45 from Mendoza (no stops).
Puente del Inca → Parque Provincial Aconcagua - Centro de Visitantes Horcones (Laguna de Horcones)3 km5 minRN7 + desvío señalizado a la derecha (500 m) · asfalto/ripio cortoOptional (+6 km round trip on top of the day's 374). Parking at the Visitor Centre at 2,950 m; from there the short trail to Laguna de Horcones and the Aconcagua viewpoint is easy, 1 h round trip walking slowly. Day ticket: see 'entradas'.
Horcones → Las Cuevas (arco / portal de Las Cuevas)15 km15 minRN7 · asfaltoOptional (+30 km round trip). Las Cuevas (3,150 m) is the last village before the international tunnel: stone arch, alpine-style houses, little else. From there the 8 km gravel road to Cristo Redentor (3,850 m) starts, almost always still closed by snow in November (see tips). Cold and windy: 5 min for the photo and back.
Las Cuevas / Puente del Inca → Uspallata (almuerzo tardío)85 km1 h 15RN7 (bajada) · asfaltoDescent with good visibility; use engine braking on the long Penitentes-Polvaredas grades. With the proposed sequence (Puente del Inca 12:15, Horcones 12:45-13:45, Las Cuevas 14:00) you reach Uspallata ≈ 15:45 for a sit-down lunch; La Juanita serves until 17:30 and El Rancho all day.
Uspallata → Hualta Hotel (Mendoza)117 km1 h 45RN7 → Acceso Sur / RP82 → Av. San Martín · asfaltoLeaving Uspallata at 17:00 you reach Mendoza 18:45-19:00 in daylight (sunset ≈ 20:30 in November). Holiday: late afternoon many people return from Potrerillos; if RN7 is busy, RP82 via Cacheuta is the alternative. Day total: 374 km (Mendoza-Puente del Inca round trip) + 36 km if you add Horcones and Las Cuevas.

🎫 Tickets and opening hours

  • Parque Provincial Aconcagua - visita diaria a la Quebrada / Laguna de Horcones · 💲 ARS 10.000 p.p. (temporada 1 nov 2025 - 30 abr 2026, decreto 2322/25). Sin cargo: menores de 12, personas con discapacidad y jubilados/pensionados residentes en Argentina (Néstor y Ana: llevar DNI y constancia de jubilación; la exención habla de residentes, puede que no la acepten). La tarifa 2026-27 sale por decreto nuevo en octubre-noviembre de 2026: verificar. · 🕒 temporada estival desde el 1 de noviembre; ingreso de día aprox. 08:00-17:00 (en 2024: 10:00-16:00). El sendero puede cerrarse por nieve o viento. — Buy online before leaving (no signal in the mountains): pick 'Parque Provincial Aconcagua', activity 'visita diaria / Laguna de Horcones', date 23/11, enter the 3 visitors, download the coupon and pay with Mercado Pago or Pago Facil; the receipt arrives by email. Per the government (2025) tickets are not sold on site at natural areas. Keep the PDF or a screenshot on your phone. · 🔗 official
  • Puente del Inca · 💲 gratis · 🕒 libre — No ticket; free parking in the village. Viewing only from the lookout: walking on the bridge is forbidden. · 🔗 official
  • Camino al Cristo Redentor (Las Cuevas) · 💲 gratis · 🕒 abre cuando Vialidad despeja la nieve (históricamente entre el 10 de diciembre y mediados de enero) · cerrado en invierno — Assume closed on 23 November. If you want to try, check the status at vialidad.mendoza.gov.ar or with the Gendarmeria post in Las Cuevas that day. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Moved holiday (Mon 23 Nov): heavy local traffic towards Potrerillos and Uspallata from 10:00 and back 17:00-20:00. Leaving 08:30 keeps you ahead; returning via RP82 (Cacheuta) helps if RN7 is busy.
  • Fuel: full tank in Mendoza; top up at the YPF in central Uspallata. From there to Las Cuevas and back (176 km) there is nothing.
  • Altitude: from 750 m (Mendoza) to 2,950 m (Horcones) and 3,150 m (Las Cuevas) in one morning. Walk slowly, drink water, no alcohol at lunch; if anyone gets a headache, descend. Coca leaves or coca candy are sold at the Puente del Inca fair.
  • Weather: Puente del Inca/Las Cuevas can be 5-10 C with strong afternoon wind even when Mendoza is at 30 C: jacket, hat and sunglasses. Sun at 3,000 m burns in 20 minutes: sunscreen.
  • Documents: Gendarmeria at Punta de Vacas and Las Cuevas may ask for ID and the vehicle papers; keep the Ranger's driving authorisation handy if it is not in your name.
  • Food: mountain options are basic with unreliable hours. Plan A: coffee in Uspallata going up and a late lunch (15:45) at La Juanita coming down. Plan B: the Puente del Inca inn's dining room at 13:00 (unverified). Carry fruit, crackers and water in the Raptor just in case.
  • Cash: the Puente del Inca fair and mountain eateries are usually cash only; no mobile signal between Uspallata and Las Cuevas, download offline maps.
  • If the Cristo Redentor road is closed (most likely), the Aconcagua lookout from Horcones is the photo of the day: at 12:30-13:30 the south face is lit.

  • Visitas y almuerzos en bodegas del Valle de Uco (martes) · 💲 degustaciones ≈ US$ 18-40 p.p.; almuerzos con maridaje ≈ US$ 50-100 p.p. según bodega (estimaciones 2026; cada bodega confirma el precio al reservar) · 🕒 Andeluna mar-dom 10:00-20:00 · La Azul mar-dom 10:30-18:00 · Domaine Bousquet lun-dom 09:00-17:30 · Salentein todos los días (Killka 12:30-15:30) · Zuccardi todos los días (almuerzo 12:30) — ALL require advance booking (some will not open the gate without one). Book at least 48 h ahead by email/WhatsApp stating 3 adults, time and that there is a designated driver; a card deposit is often requested. Those closed on Mondays (Andeluna, La Azul) do open on Tuesdays. · 🔗 official
  • Viator 246702P2 - tour al Valle de Uco (alternativa sin manejar) · 💲 a confirmar en Viator · 🕒 día completo con búsqueda en el hotel — If you would rather not drive after tasting, Viator product 246702P2 remains as the alternative (not booked; the link is Viator's search by product code, the listing itself was not verified). Check date and time on Viator before booking; with a tour you do not need winery reservations. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Designated driver: zero alcohol at the wheel (national law 27.714) and checkpoints on RN40 and RP89 on weekends and holidays. Whoever drives the Raptor does not taste: Carolina (18) can drive back if the Ranger's authorisation covers her; otherwise Nestor sips and spits (wineries have spittoons and consider it normal).
  • Bookings: make them today (Sat 21 or Sun 22) by WhatsApp/email. Tuesday is quiet in the Uco Valley, but winery restaurants have few covers and a single lunch seating (12:30-13:00).
  • Fuel: full tank leaving Mendoza; do not count on refuelling in Tupungato.
  • Sun and heat: 32-35 C at midday in the valley; hat, water and sunscreen. Wineries sit at 1,100-1,300 m: evenings cool down.
  • Relaxed pace: one tasting (11:00) + one lunch (13:00) fits comfortably; three wineries in a day means rushing. The Cordon del Plata view from the Gualtallary terraces is the best in the valley.
  • Last night in Mendoza: pack before dinner; Wednesday you leave for San Juan (165 km) with a 12:00 check-out.

🎫 Tickets and opening hours

  • Casa Natal de Sarmiento – Museo Nacional · 💲 gratis · 🕒 lun, mar, jue–dom y feriados 09:00–19:00; miércoles cerrado; visitas guiadas 10:00, 12:00, 15:00 y 18:00 — No booking, first come first served (25 per guided visit). Closed on 25 Nov (Wednesday): go Thursday 26 at 10:00. · 🔗 official
  • Museo Provincial de Bellas Artes Franklin Rawson · 💲 ARS 1.000 · jubilados y estudiantes 500 · menores de 6 y domingos gratis (abr 2026) · 🕒 mar–dom 12:00–20:00 — Pay at the desk; bring ID for the senior discount. · 🔗 official
  • Museo Santiago Graffigna · 💲 a confirmar (≈ ARS 7.000 con degustación según reseña 2025) · 🕒 jue–sáb, visitas guiadas con cupo (11:15–16:15 según Google; 09:30–17:30 según agenda abr 2026) — Closed on Wednesdays. Book by phone 264 421-4227 ext. 134 or 121. · 🔗 official
  • Museo de Ciencias Naturales / MUPA – Museo Paleontológico de San Juan · 💲 no aplica (no está abierto en las fechas del viaje) · 🕒 inaugura el 16 de diciembre de 2026 (Diario Huarpe, 26 oct 2026) — The Ischigualasto dinosaur museum in the city (Predio Ferial / former Belgrano station, Av. España between 25 de Mayo and Félix Aguilar) is finished but opens only on 16 Dec 2026; the old Museo de Ciencias Naturales hall is not open to the public. The real fossils are on show at the William Sill site museum inside Ischigualasto park (day 7, free). · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Wednesday in San Juan: Sarmiento's birthplace and the Graffigna museum are closed. Afternoon plan: Cathedral bell tower (from 16:00) and Franklin Rawson museum (12–20), then the square and pedestrian street after 18:00.
  • Real siesta 13:00–17:00: shops shut and streets empty; dinner places open only at 20:30–21:00 (Casa España at 19:00 is the exception).
  • Heat: 35 °C in the afternoon in November. Water in the car, hat, sunscreen; walk before 11 or after 18.
  • Fuel: fill up at Media Agua (AXION) or Pocito (YPF Full) before entering the city; tomorrow it is 155 km to the next YPF (Jáchal).
  • Apartment check-in from 14:00: have lunch first (Palito opens 12:30) and move in afterwards; ask the host where to leave the Raptor (garage, not street).
  • If you want Sarmiento's house, the only slot is Thursday 26 at 10:00 (guided visit, 45 min) before leaving for Jáchal.
  • Cash: cards work almost everywhere in downtown San Juan, but withdraw pesos here because from Jáchal onwards ATMs are scarce and many places are cash only.

Day 6 · Thu Nov 26 · San Juan → Jáchal → Huaco pass → Guandacol → Villa Unión 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Villa Unión · 303 km

🧭 How to get there

LegkmTimeRoadNotes
San Juan (depto, centro) → San José de Jáchal (Plaza San Martín)155 km2 h 00RN40 · asfaltoLeave via Av. Rioja / Av. Rawson and Acceso Norte (RN40) through Chimbas (YPF Centenario, 24 h, on the way out of the city). After Albardón come 130 km of RN40 past Talacasto and Niquivil: rolling hills, long straights and no services until Jáchal. Guanacos, donkeys and goats near the shoulder; crosswinds in the afternoon. You enter Jáchal on RN150 (last 10 km, roundabout) and Av. Santiago Funes: the YPF ACA is there at the edge of town, the last reliable fuel of the day. OSRM: 157.8 km / 2 h 16 (conservative).
Jáchal → Mirador Cuesta de Huaco (RP491)29 km40 minRP491 (desvío de la RN40) · asfaltoThis is a detour: direct RN40 runs across the flats (51 km Jáchal–Huaco); RP491 climbs past the Los Cauquenes dam and La Ciénaga to the Huaco pass, a narrow mountain road with tight curves and no shoulder. Take it slow (40–60 km/h): it is the prettiest stretch of the day. The lookout is at the top, with a dirt pull-off; watch loose rocks when you get out. OSRM: 29.3 km / 43 min.
Mirador Cuesta de Huaco → Huaco (Molino Viejo y empalme RN40)8 km15 minRP491 · asfaltoShort descent into the Huaco valley: poplars, adobe houses and the Old Mill (1770s, national monument) at the entrance to the village. From Huaco you rejoin RN40 northbound. The full pass detour adds about 5 km and 20–25 min versus direct RN40.
Huaco → Guandacol (La Rioja)70 km55 minRN40 · asfaltoDesert straight with reddish hills; you cross the San Juan–La Rioja border (police post, vehicle papers are sometimes checked). No shade or services. Guandacol is a small town with a nice square; its unbranded fuel station is unreliable (runs dry, bank-transfer only): do not count on it.
Guandacol → Villa Unión (Casa Los Abuelos, Honorato Guerrero y Av. Alem)44 km35 minRN40 y RN76 · asfaltoStay on RN40 for 39 km to the roundabout south of Villa Unión; RN76 starts there and enters town as Av. Nicolás Dávila. The 24 h YPF is on that avenue 1.5 km before the house; then right on Av. Gral. Perón and left on Honorato Guerrero. Casa Los Abuelos is 350 m from the main square. OSRM: 46.6 km / 46 min from Guandacol's square.

💡 Tips

  • Checkout at 11:00 is the deadline, not the departure time: leaving at 09:00 gets you to Jáchal at 11:00 with time for coffee at Edesia, semitas at El Sema and a relaxed lunch at 12:30; leaving at 11:00 lands you at 13:00 in full siesta.
  • If you take the Sarmiento house visit (Thursday 10:00, free guided tour), check out at 09:45, park near Sarmiento Sur 21 and leave at 11:00.
  • Fuel: full tank at the YPF ACA in Jáchal. Guandacol does not count. Next YPF: Villa Unión.
  • Jáchal at midday is thin: the good restaurants open at night. Lo de Pedro or Parrilla Mary; call ahead.
  • Huaco pass: detour via RP491, narrow mountain asphalt. Adds 20–25 min versus direct RN40. In the Raptor keep to 40–60 km/h and do not stop on the curves.
  • 35 °C in the afternoon in La Rioja; the Huaco–Villa Unión stretch has no shade or services: water and air conditioning.
  • Arrival ≈ 16:00 at Casa Los Abuelos: Graciela welcomes you; covered garage for the Raptor. El Negro supermarket opens at 18:00: shop, then dinner at 1833 Bistró (opens 18:00, book).
  • Cash: in Villa Unión and Guandacol many shops are cash only and the town ATM runs dry on long weekends; bring pesos from San Juan.

🎫 Tickets and opening hours

  • Parque Provincial Ischigualasto – circuito tradicional (vehículo propio en caravana, 40 km, 3 h) · 💲 ARS 45.000 argentinos · 14.000 jubilados y estudiantes del resto del país · 65.000 extranjeros · menores de 6 gratis (Res. 070-APPI-2026, vigente desde 1 jul 2026) · 🕒 08:00–17:00, ingresos cada hora (web oficial); temporada otoño-invierno 2026 fue 09:00–16:00; con calor extremo: ingresos hasta las 11:00 y luego 16:00 y 17:00 — Bought at the gate ticket office in order of arrival; no online sales or booking for the traditional circuit (only full-moon and alternative circuits are booked: reservas.ischigualasto@gmail.com, 264 418-6119). Payment method not confirmed in 2026 sources: carry cash for the tickets (3 people ≈ ARS 73,000–135,000 depending on the category applied). Site museum free. Optional private guide ARS 70,000. · 🔗 official
  • Circuito con luna llena · 💲 ARS 47.000 (desde 1 jul 2026) · 🕒 solo 4 noches por mes alrededor de la luna llena (2 antes y 1 después, web oficial); la luna llena de noviembre 2026 cae ≈ 24 nov (verificar en el calendario lunar del parque), así que el 27 ya no se hace — Not applicable on this trip: besides, driving back to Villa Unión at night on RN76 (138 km with animals on the road) is not advisable. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Timing: the official site warns that in high heat entries stop at 11:00 and resume only at 16:00. Be there by 10:20 for the 11:00 convoy; if you miss it the next may be at 16:00, which wrecks the day. For more margin leave at 07:45 for the 10:00 one.
  • Fuel: full tank at the Villa Unión YPF on the way out. Nothing en route or at the park. A full tank is plenty: 275 km of road plus the 40 km circuit.
  • Heat and sun: 35 °C at midday, no shade at the stops. 1.5 L of water per person, hat, sunscreen, closed shoes (sand and rock), sunglasses. Walks are 10–20 min each, flat.
  • Dust on the circuit: windows up, AC on, camera stowed between stops. The Raptor is more than enough; you drive at 20–40 km/h behind the guide, no overtaking or leaving the track.
  • Cash: ticket office (payment method unconfirmed), the Los Baldecitos comedor, craft stalls. No phone signal from Pagancillo to the park: tell the house what time you will be back.
  • Pensioner rate: bring Argentine ID and proof of retirement; with only a US passport you will be charged the foreigner rate (65,000).
  • Back in daylight: leave the park by 14:30 at the latest, lunch at Los Baldecitos, home 17:30. No sunset at the park for anyone sleeping in Villa Unión.
  • Talampaya is 59 km along the same road; if you want it another day it is a separate park (mandatory bus, no private cars inside).

Day 8 · Sat Nov 28 · Villa Unión → Cuesta de Miranda → Chilecito → Villa Unión 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Villa Unión · 222 km

🧭 How to get there

LegkmTimeRoadNotes
Villa Unión (Casa Los Abuelos, Honorato Guerrero s/n) → Mirador Cuesta de Miranda – Bordo Atravesado (RN40, ≈ 2.020 m)67 km1 h 00RN76 (3 km) + RN40 este · asfaltoFill up at the YPF at the Villa Unión entrance (RN76) before leaving. After 3 km you join RN40 eastbound; flat until Puerto Alegre, then the climb starts. From Los Tambillos the Cuesta de Miranda proper begins: 11.5 km of curves, fully paved (rebuilt and paved 2011–2015; OSM tags it asphalt). Gravel shoulders, concrete fords over dry riverbeds (after rain they can run water: never cross moving water). Loose goats and donkeys. OSRM says 48 min; with the climb and photo stops count 1 h.

Famatina range to the north, Sañogasta range to the south. You enter Chilecito from the south on Av. Presidente Perón: the YPF and Cable Car Station 1 are right there.
Chilecito → Villa Unión (Casa Los Abuelos)111 km1 h 45RN40 oeste (Nonogasta – Cuesta de Miranda) + RN76 · asfaltoSame road back. Leave Chilecito by 17:00–17:15 at the latest: you reach the pass 17:45–18:15 with afternoon light full on the red walls of the west side (best photo of the day) and you are in Villa Unión before 19:30, in daylight (sunset in La Rioja in late November ≈ 20:10). Do not drive the pass after dark: animals and fords.

Sales room and tasting; the plant tour depends on staff that day. · 🔗 official
  • Museo del Cablecarril – Estación 1 · 💲 gratis / contribución voluntaria · 🕒 no publicado (ver parada 4) — No booking; you go in with the municipal guide. If closed, the ore carts and towers are visible from the street anyway. · 🔗 official
  • Samay Huasi (museo UNLP) · 💲 bono contribución, a confirmar (+54 3825-422629) · 🕒 sáb 8:00–12:00 y 14:00–18:00 (verificar) — Cash. No booking needed for three people. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Day order that fits Saturday hours: 08:30 leave · 09:30 pass viewpoint · 10:45 La Riojana (closes 13:00) · 12:00 cable car museum · 13:00 lunch · 15:00 Samay Huasi (reopens 14:00) · 16:30 coffee + fuel · 17:00 drive back.
  • Saturday + siesta: 13:00–17:00 Chilecito is shut except restaurants; do not leave shopping for the afternoon.
  • Cuesta de Miranda is paved end to end (2015): any car does it; 40–60 km/h in the curves, gravel shoulders, fords. Loose animals the whole way.
  • Heat: 33–36 °C at midday in Chilecito in late November; water in the car, hat, sunscreen. The pass is cool in the morning.
  • Fuel: fill in Villa Unión on departure (YPF RN76) and in Chilecito before returning (YPF Av. Perón). In between the only pump is at Nonogasta.
  • Cash: La Riojana and restaurants take cards, but the cable car museum and Samay Huasi run on cash donations; carry ARS 30,000 in small notes.
  • Police checkpoint on RN40 near Nonogasta: car papers at hand and the invoice for any wine you buy.
  • No mobile signal on the pass: download the offline map and tell the house what time you will be back.
  • Afternoon light (17:45–18:30) is best for the red walls on the Villa Unión side; in the morning they are in shade.

(talampaya.com) · 🕒 adicional a las salidas de 09:00 y 13:30; 1 h 30, 2,3 km — Strict age limit 10 to 65 and an uphill walk in the sun: outside this trip's scope. 💡 Tips

  • Book the 29/11 09:00 Experiencia Tradicional on talampaya.com several days ahead (limited seats, Sunday) and buy the 3 APN tickets at ventaweb.apn.gob.ar: two separate payments.
  • Carry both vouchers printed or on your phone: there is no mobile signal in the park.
  • Leave 07:45; check-in 08:30; tour 09:00–11:30; lunch 12:00; home 14:00; pool. If you would rather sleep in, the 16:00 departure has the best light (back 19:30, in daylight) and you lunch at leisure in Villa Unión.
  • Heat: 35 °C at noon in the canyon in late November; at 09:00 it is 22–25 °C. Water (1 litre per person), hat, sunscreen, closed shoes: short walks on sand.
  • Fuel: none at the park or in Pagancillo; fill up at the Villa Unión YPF. 134 km, a quarter tank for the Raptor.
  • Cash: park entry on site is cash or debit only; the restaurant and craft fair may have no card terminal. Carry ARS 60,000–80,000.
  • Retiree discount: only with an Argentine DNI and residence in the country; check which documents Néstor and Ana carry to avoid an argument at the ticket office.
  • If it rained in the hills, the riverbeds fill within hours and the park suspends tours: check the forecast Saturday night and confirm by WhatsApp.
  • The house has a pool: plan the afternoon there; tomorrow (day 10) you leave 08:15 with 10:00 checkout and 327 km.

Fords and animals as always. Arrive Chilecito ≈ 10:00: coffee on the square and a full tank at the YPF on Av. Perón, since it is another 216 km to Belén with uncertain pumps.
Chilecito → Pituil70 km50 minRN40 norte · asfaltoLeave Chilecito north on RN40 skirting the Famatina range (the Nevado, 6,000 m, on your left; snow on top until December). Olive and vine villages: Famatina lies off to the side (RP11), Pituil is the last Riojan village with shops. OSRM: 70.1 km · 53 min. Nothing to stop for except a photo of Famatina.
Pituil → Londres (Catamarca)119 km1 h 25RN40 norte (Alpasinche – San Blas de los Sauces – límite con Catamarca) · asfaltoLong straight stretch along the valley: Campanas, Alpasinche, Salicas and San Blas de los Sauces (fuel station, useful backup), then the Catamarca border and down to Londres, the country's second-oldest town (1558). RN40 here has frequent concrete fords: summer storms start in November and can bring water or mud; if water is running, wait. OSRM gives ≈ 2 h for this stretch because it penalises the fords; at normal pace it is 1 h 25.
Londres (plaza) → El Shincal de Quimivil7 km15 mincalle 9 de Julio hacia el oeste (RP219 / camino al Shincal) · asfalto + últimos km de ripio consolidadoFrom RN40 (Shincal access ≈ km 74, outskirts of Londres) take calle 9 de Julio west: 6.6 km of wide, level road with a final gravel stretch fine for any car. Best done this afternoon: you reach Londres ≈ 13:00, after the last morning guided visit (11:00–11:30), so you carry on to Belén for lunch and come back for the 16:00 departure (25 km · 25 min from the house).
El Shincal / Londres → Belén (Huaco country house, calle Urquiza s/n)20 km20 minRN40 norte · asfaltoLondres to Belén is 14 km on RN40 (you pass the statue of founder Juan Pérez de Zurita at the north tip of Londres; Belén is at km 86.8). From El Shincal, 20 km · 20 min (OSRM 19.8 km · 23 min). Belén, 1,250 m: the town with all services in the area. Huaco check-in 15:00 with lockbox; calle Urquiza is the same street as restaurant 1900.

📍 El Shincal de Quimivil – sitio arqueológico inca (visita guiada 16:00) · Londres
Camino al Shincal (calle 9 de Julio al oeste de la RN40), 6,6 km de la plaza de Londres, Dpto. Belén, Catamarca · 🕒 Abre todos los días, lunes incluido (Google: 8:00–20:00; TripAdvisor: lun 8:00–18:30). Solo con guía, a horarios fijos — las fuentes DISCREPAN: visitcatamarca.com (2026) dice 8:00 · 9:30 · 11:00 y 16:00 · 17:30 · 18:30; turismoruta40 (jul 2025) dice 9:00 · 10:00 · 11:30 y 14:30 · 16:00 · 17:30. La de las 16:00 figura en ambas: apuntar a esa y CONFIRMAR por teléfono el domingo: 3835 534050 · 3835 431437 (IG @shincaldequimivil) · 💲 ARS 1.500 p.p. en dic 2024 (reseña TripAdvisor); 2026 a confirmar — efectivo
Argentina's most important Inca city (1471–1536): ceremonial plaza, kallankas, ushnu (platform), storehouses and two hills with stone stairways overlooking the whole valley; part of the Qhapaq Ñan World Heritage route. Interpretation centre and site museum at the entrance, accessible toilets, rest areas and a small café. Compulsory guided visit of 1 h 30–2 h, easy walk with a short climb up a hill (optional, you can wait below). Ask for Rosa ('Rosita', guide since 1998), Dahlia or Mayra. The only site in the region with an accessible circuit (adapted chairs) if Ana or Néstor prefer not to walk.

💡 Tips

  • Proposed schedule: 08:15 leave · 10:00 Chilecito (coffee + fuel) · 10:40 on · 13:00 Londres · 13:20 lunch in Belén (1900) · 15:00 Huaco check-in · 15:30 leave for El Shincal · 16:00–17:45 guided visit · 18:15 Belén · 19:30 Virgin on the hill · 21:00 dinner.
  • El Shincal: call on SUNDAY at 3835 534050 to confirm Monday has a 16:00 visit (sources disagree: 14:30 or 16:00) and the 2026 price; no entry without a guide.
  • Checkout 10:00 in Villa Unión but leave 08:00–08:30: every half hour of delay pushes lunch against 1900's 15:00 closing.
  • Fuel: fill in Chilecito (YPF Av. Perón). Backup, San Blas de los Sauces. Belén has a pump but no confirmed brand; Catamarca had shortages in 2026.
  • Fords: between Pituil and Belén RN40 crosses dozens of dry riverbeds on concrete fords; afternoon storms send water and mud down them. Never cross running water.
  • Cash: El Shincal, the Londres museum and the weavers take cash; Belén restaurants accept cards but check the bill.
  • Heat and sun: 33–35 °C in the afternoon at Londres; El Shincal is open-air with a short stairway: water, hat, sneakers. By 16:00 the sun eases a little.
  • Monday: many Belén shops close (RestoBar Ruta 40 closed). Dinner secured at 1900 (Urquiza 300, steps from the house).
  • Tuesday breakfast: I could not confirm a bakery in Belén; buy something at La Chiquita (Chilecito) on the way or ask the Huaco host.
  • Patchy mobile signal between San Blas and Londres: offline maps and tell Huaco your estimated arrival time.

Day 11 · Tue Dec 1 · Belén → Hualfín → Santa María → Quilmes → Cafayate 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Cafayate · 250 km

🧭 How to get there

LegkmTimeRoadNotes
Belén (Huaco country house, calle Urquiza s/n) → Hualfín (desvío a las termas)63 km50 minRN40 · asfaltoCheckout is 10:00 but leave 08:30–09:00 and drop the key as the host says. Fill up in Belén before leaving (last sizable town). RN40 is paved all the way to Santa María, with gravel shoulders and concrete fords across dry riverbeds: slow down at each ford. You pass the RP43 turn-off to Antofagasta de la Sierra at El Eje. Hualfín: a 1770 chapel (national monument) and 32 °C hot springs in the gorge a few km off the road on a dirt track; a quick look only, not a soak, with the day ahead.
Hualfín → Santa María (Catamarca)110 km1 h 25RN40 · asfaltoYou climb to the section's high point (2,277 m at Los Nacimientos) and cross the Campo del Arenal: high plain, wind and no services for about 60 km. Speed checks and loose animals (donkeys, goats) near the hamlets. Arrival at Santa María (1,880 m) for a sit-down lunch on the plaza. Cumulative from Belén: 173 km · 2 h 15.
Santa María → Ciudad Sagrada de Quilmes22 km20 minRN40 + acceso de tierra 5 km · asfalto + ripioYou enter Tucumán. The turn-off to the ruins is signposted on the left of RN40, about 3 km north of the RP307 junction (the road from Amaicha/Tafí). The last 5 km are packed dirt, no issue for the Raptor; keep to 40 km/h because of dust. Cumulative: 195 km.
Ciudad Sagrada de Quilmes → Cafayate (Bright house, Vicario Toscano 1230)55 km40 minRN40 · asfaltoBack on RN40 heading north along the Santa María river valley: Colalao del Valle, the Salta border at Tolombón, and into Cafayate from the south (Av. Güemes Sur). The YPF is on RN40 at the southern entrance: fill up there so the tank is full for the next days. Check-in 15:00 via lockbox (the host sends the code). Day total: 250 km.

  • Cafayate: 15:00 lockbox check-in; dine at 20:30 since nothing opens earlier; El Rancho and Pacha close Mondays (1 Dec is a Tuesday, fine).
  • Shop for breakfast on the afternoon of day 1: shops close for siesta 13:00–17:00.

Day 12 · Wed Dec 2 · Quebrada de las Conchas by car and wineries on foot in Cafayate 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Cafayate · 110 km

Cafayate (Bright house) → Los Médanos · Las Ventanas · Los Castillos · El Obelisco27 km35 minRN68 norte · asfaltoLeave 08:30 while the sun is still low (the reds look best in the morning and there are fewer minibuses). Garganta del Diablo (con mirador Tres Cruces opcional) → Cafayate (centro)60 km55 minRN68 sur · asfaltoOptional: continue 5 km north to the Tres Cruces viewpoint (panorama of the whole gorge, short dirt access) and turn around there: those are the extra 10 km that make up the day's ≈ 110 km. 💡 Tips

  • Leave 08:30: the gorge fills with minibuses from Salta after 11:00.
  • No fuel or signal in the gorge; full tank and water in the car.
  • Loose animals (goats, donkeys) and blind bends on RN68: 60–80 km/h, no hurry.
  • The town wineries are done on foot: El Esteco and Vasija Secreta together to the north; Nanni and Domingo Hermanos 2–3 blocks from the plaza.
  • Wine: buy at the winery and carry it in the Raptor; it costs more in Salta.
  • Book El Esteco by WhatsApp a day ahead; Pacha and Güemes 125 via Meitre or phone.
  • Miranda opens 13:00: ideal after lunch, before siesta.

LegkmTimeRoadNotes
Cafayate (Bright house) → Piattelli Vineyards (RP2 km 3)4 km10 minRP2 (camino a Yacochuya) · asfaltoThe base day's only driving: 4 km west on the Yacochuya road, climbing to the winery overlooking the valley. 8 km round trip. If you would rather not drive after wine, a remís from the plaza is cheap.

Angastaco (12 km further) has a simple roadhouse, but the sit-down lunch is better back in Cafayate. Time estimated with the 50 % gravel surcharge; OSRM was not available for this run.
OPTIONAL · Quebrada de las Flechas → Cafayate60 km1 h 15RN40 sur · ripio + asfaltoReturn the same way: 120 km round trip, 2 h 30 net driving, 72 km of it gravel. Full tank (no fuel between Cafayate and Cachi) and tyres checked before leaving.

💡 Tips

  • A real rest day: sleep in, house pool and a single commitment (the booked lunch).
  • Book Piattelli 2–3 days ahead; if full, Finca Las Nubes by WhatsApp.
  • Whoever drives to Piattelli should go easy on the wine: 4 km back with frequent police checks at the town entrance.
  • Quebrada de las Flechas only if you leave 08:30: 72 km of gravel, no fuel or signal, and back for lunch at 13:00.
  • Siesta: almost everything closes 13:00–17:00; see the cathedral in the morning or at 18:00.
  • You leave Cafayate tomorrow: fill the Raptor today (YPF at the southern entrance).
  • Laundry and wine shopping to take to Salta: do it today, Friday is an early start.

Day 14 · Fri Dec 4 · Cafayate → Alemanía → Cabra Corral → Salta 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Salta · 189 km

🧭 How to get there

LegkmTimeRoadNotes
Cafayate (Bright house, Vicario Toscano 1230) → Alemanía (estación)95 km1 h 30RN68 norte · asfaltoCheckout and departure 08:30–09:00 with a full tank (YPF at the southern entrance). You cross the whole Quebrada de las Conchas again: today no stops except a quick photo at Tres Cruces or La Yesera (≈ km 55–60), left out on Wednesday. After Garganta del Diablo the gorge opens up and at 95 km the 1 km turn-off to Alemanía is on the left, across the old bridge over the Las Conchas river. Bends, loose cows and goats; speed check before Alemanía.
Alemanía → Coronel Moldes (cruce RP47 al dique)45 km40 minRN68 norte · asfaltoLerma valley: you pass La Viña and the Posta de las Cabras (RN68 km ≈ 100, goat cheese and sweets for a 10-minute stop). At Coronel Moldes take RP47 right toward the Cabra Corral dam (12 paved km to the bridge). Cumulative from Cafayate: 140 km.
OPTIONAL · Coronel Moldes → Dique Cabra Corral (almuerzo) y vuelta a la RN6824 km35 minRP47 ida y vuelta · asfaltoOptional 24 km round-trip detour NOT included in the day's 189 km: 12 km to the lakeside restaurants (km 9.5 and km 12 of RP47) and the dam bridge, overlooking Salta's largest reservoir. Sit-down lunch 12:30–14:30 and back to RN68.
Coronel Moldes → Salta (Sheraton, Coronel Francisco de Uriondo)49 km50 minRN68 norte → El Carril → Av. Circunvalación / acceso este · asfaltoFlat stretch with growing traffic from El Carril (YPF on RN68 if needed). Into Salta from the south; the Sheraton is at the eastern edge, at the foot of Cerro San Bernardo next to Parque San Martín and the cable-car base. Check-in 15:00; covered hotel parking with a charge (ARS 8,600/night per the brief; Marriott lists 10,000: confirm at reception). Day total: 189 km (213 with the dam detour).

💡 Tips

  • Saturday 5 starts the long weekend (Mon 7 and Tue 8 are holidays): Salta fills up; book the peña today and do the MAAM first thing.
  • Suggested order: 09:00 breakfast · 10:00–11:30 MAAM (confirm whether it opens 10 or 11) · San Francisco and San Bernardo · 12:30 lunch · hotel siesta · 17:30 cable car · 21:00 peña.
  • Downtown is all flat walking; the only climb is back to the Sheraton, which is uphill: taxi.
  • Balcarce peñas start the show at 22:00 and go on until 02:00; there is no early dinner, arrive 21:00 and order empanadas while it starts.
  • Coca: leaves are sold at Mercado San Miguel; useful for the altitude in Humahuaca over the next days.

Day 16 · Sun Dec 6 🎉 · Salta → Jujuy → Purmamarca → Huacalera 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Huacalera · 223 km

💡 Tips

  • Sunday of a long weekend (Mon 7 bridge + Tue 8 holiday): Purmamarca is packed 11–17. Arriving at 11:30 you can still park; book lunch.
  • Fuel: full tank in Jujuy. Purmamarca has no station; the only one before Humahuaca is YPF Tilcara (queues). Tomorrow there is no fuel on RN52 to Salinas.
  • Altitude: Purmamarca 2,200 m, Huacalera 2,650 m. First day up high: go slow, drink lots of water, light lunch, go easy on alcohol. Coca sweets or tea help.
  • Cash: the fair, toilets and many Purmamarca shops take no cards or have no signal. Get pesos in Salta or Jujuy; Quebrada ATMs run dry on long weekends.
  • Sun: at 2,500 m it burns in 20 minutes. Hat, sunglasses and sunscreen before the Paseo de los Colorados.
  • Check-in 14:00. If you arrive before 16:00, the hotel pool is the best plan for the afternoon.
  • For Sunday dinner in Tilcara the verified option is La Chacana (open daily). El Nuevo Progreso and Khuska close on Sundays.

🎫 Tickets and opening hours

  • Salinas Grandes — recorrido guiado comunitario · 💲 ≈ ARS 8.000–10.000 p.p. (jul 2026: 10.000; mar 2026: 6.000; nov 2025: 4.000 piletones / 8.000 Ojo del Salar) · baños 500 · solo efectivo · 🕒 de día; salidas continuas a medida que se arman grupos (1 h) — Paid at the post, cash, no booking. The fee changes every season: carry ARS 40,000 in small notes for the three of you plus toilets. No ATM, no signal. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Leave at 09:00 sharp: by 10:30 you are at Salinas under a clear sky; after noon clouds and wind build and the Salta/Jujuy tour vans arrive in packs.
  • Fuel: full tank at YPF Tilcara (better the afternoon before). Not a single pump in 130 km of RN52; the climb burns much more.
  • Altitude: 4,170 m at the pass, 3,450 m on the salt flat. Light breakfast, 2 L of water each, coca sweets, move slowly. If anyone feels bad, going down is the cure.
  • Sun and wind: salt reflects like snow. Dark sunglasses (a must), hat, SPF 50 and a windbreaker even if the car is warm.
  • Cash: guide, toilets and crafts in pesos only, no signal. No ATM after Tilcara.
  • On the flat walk where the guide walks: there are soft spots and pools. After recent rain there is 2–5 cm of water: old trainers or rubber sandals.
  • The Raptor does not drive onto the flat on its own: only in the community convoy, on the marked track.
  • Bridge Monday: the Pucará de Tilcara is closed (open Tue–Sun); that is why today is Salinas and tomorrow Tilcara.

🎫 Tickets and opening hours

  • Pucará de Tilcara (UBA) · 💲 general ARS 12.000 · residentes argentinos 6.000 · jubilados gratis · menores de 12 gratis · 🕒 mar–dom 09:00–18:30, último ingreso 17:15; lunes cerrado — Paid at the site ticket desk (cash for sure; card to be confirmed).   • Garganta del Diablo (comunidad de Tilcara) · 💲 ≈ ARS 3.000–5.000 p.p. (2025–2026) · efectivo · 🕒 ≈ 09:00–18:00 — Paid and signed in at the yellow hut by the car park. No ATM or signal. Fee changes often. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Tuesday 8 holiday (Immaculate Conception): Tilcara fills with Salta and Jujuy day-trippers from 11. Pucará at 09:00, Garganta before 11:30, lunch booked for 13:00.
  • Retirees: free Pucará entry with proof of pension; passport only = general ARS 12,000 (still cheap).
  • Pucará: stone paths with steps and 80 m of climb at 2,500 m; closed shoes, hat, water. Rest in the shade of the cardón cacti.
  • Garganta del Diablo: single-lane gravel with hairpins, nothing technical for the Raptor but go slowly and sound the horn on blind bends; the one going down yields.
  • Waterfall: only for the sure-footed (loose stones and stream crossings). Lookout and dam are for everyone.
  • Cash for both community entries and the stalls; Tilcara has an ATM near the plaza (to confirm) but it runs dry on holidays: arrive with pesos.
  • Maimará: the Paleta del Pintor looks best in afternoon sun (15–17). Leaving lunch at 15:00 is perfect timing.
  • Siesta: many Tilcara shops close 13:30–17:00 even on holidays; the plaza fair does not.

Day 19 · Wed Dec 9 · Huacalera → Uquía → Humahuaca → Hornocal Range → Huacalera 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Huacalera · 120 km

🧭 How to get there

LegkmTimeRoadNotes
Hotel Huacalera (RN9 km 1790) → Uquía (iglesia)16 km16 minRN9 norte · asfaltoLeave 09:00. OSRM: 15.8 km · 16 min. Uquía sits right on the road, on the right; park by the plaza. On the way, on the left, the sign for Viñedos Yacoraite (paraje San José).
Uquía → Humahuaca (plaza)12 km12 minRN9 norte · puente sobre el Río Grande · asfaltoOSRM: 12.2 km · 11 min (the brief counts 35 km · 35 min hotel → Humahuaca; OSRM gives 28 km · 27 min: flagged, not changed). Humahuaca is on the west bank: cross the bridge, leave the Raptor near the bus terminal/Av. Belgrano (the old centre has narrow cobbled streets, better on foot).
Humahuaca → Mirador de la Serranía del Hornocal (4.350 m)25 km45 minRP73 (ripio) hasta el desvío señalizado de 2 km al mirador · ripio con serrucho, piedra suelta y horquillas en ladera25 km of gravel: the first ≈ 15 km wide and straight across the plateau, then a ledge road with medium-difficulty hairpins; finally a signposted 2 km spur to the car park. Raptor: 4H, 30–40 km/h on the ledge, no hurry; map time plus 50% (OSRM gives 31 km · 53 min on its own trace). No fuel, no signal, no shade. Rain cuts the road: ask at the plaza tourist office or the YPF before going up.
Mirador del Hornocal → Humahuaca (almuerzo o café)25 km45 minRP73 · ripioDown in 2nd with engine braking; dust from those coming up. Round trip 1 h 30 driving plus 45 min at the top.
Humahuaca → Hotel Huacalera35 km35 minRN9 sur (YPF Humahuaca a la salida) · asfaltoFill up at YPF Humahuaca on the way out (RN9, south access): the other Quebrada station besides Tilcara. Day total 120 km. Back in daylight; in December it gets dark at 20:00.

70-tonne bronze sculpture group (Soto Avendaño, 1950) to the Army of the North, with the chasqui Pedro Socompa in front. Climb the monumental staircase from the plaza (≈ 70 steps with landings) or drive up the side street; at the top, a view of all Humahuaca and, 50 m away, the Santa Bárbara Tower (1679 Jesuit belfry Belgrano used as a fort).

The Cathedral (1631–1634, baroque interior) is opposite and opens in the morning. This sets the order: Hornocal in the morning AND Cabildo at 12 is not possible; pick one (see tips).

(reseñas jul 2026 y operador sep 2026) · efectivo · menores de 10 gratis
The folded 14-colour range at 4,761 m seen from a balcony at 4,350 m: the trip's highest point after Lipán. Main lookout right by the car park (zero effort) and a path down to a second lookout closer to the hill (8 min down, 30 min up: the older two should skip it, the air is thin). Toilets, dome with crafts and empanadas, medical post with oxygen (Dec 2025 review). LIGHT CONFLICT: the brief says go before noon; every source (todojujuy Jan 2025, jujuy.net, Jul 2026 reviews) says the best light is in the afternoon, 14:00–17:00, when the sun hits the range head-on; in the morning it is backlit. Flagged for you to decide.

🎫 Tickets and opening hours

  • Mirador del Hornocal (comunidad El Hornocal) · 💲 ≈ ARS 2.000 p.p. (jul–sep 2026) · menores de 10 gratis · efectivo · 🕒 ≈ 10:00–18:00; retirarse antes del anochecer — Cash at the car-park barrier (no formal ticket). A second ≈ 1,000 charge to walk down to the closer lookout (Aug 2025 review). No ATM or signal: bring pesos from Humahuaca. · 🔗 official
  • Iglesia de Uquía · 💲 contribución / entrada chica en efectivo (a confirmar) · 🕒 mañana y tarde, cierra en la siesta (a confirmar) — No official 2026 hours found: going in the morning (09:30) is the safe bet; if closed, ask at the shop on the plaza. · 🔗 official

💡 Tips

  • Order of the day by light (your call): A) As the brief asks: Uquía 09:30 → Humahuaca 10:15 (Monument, market) → Hornocal 11:00–12:30 (range backlit) → lunch 14:00 at Pachamanka. B) As the sources say: Uquía 09:30 → Humahuaca 10:15 → San Francisco Solano 12:00 → lunch 12:30 → Hornocal 14:30–16:00 in front light → YPF → hotel 18:00. B gives the better photo and keeps the sit-down lunch.
  • Altitude: 4,350 m at the lookout, 1,400 m above Humahuaca. Minimal effort up there, 30–45 min and down; no alcohol at lunch if going in the afternoon; water, coca and warm layers (icy wind even in sunshine).
  • Gravel: 4H, 30–40 km/h on the ledge, away from the edge on hairpins; spare wheel and tyre pressures checked at the YPF. Rain cuts RP73: ask first.
  • Cold: even if Humahuaca is 25 °C, it is 5–10 °C with wind at the top. Jacket, hat and gloves in the car.
  • Cash: Hornocal fee, Uquía church, market and toilets. ATMs in Humahuaca (plaza), but do not count on them having notes.
  • Wednesday: Pachamanka is open (closed Mondays). The market is a morning thing.
  • On the way down fill up at YPF Humahuaca: Tilcara and Humahuaca are the Quebrada's only two stations.

💡 Tips

  • Day without a clock: late breakfast, Tropic and chapel before 11 (low sun, long shadow on the sundial), pool from 12 to 17.
  • If you choose Inkillay for lunch, book days ahead and confirm it still opens on Thursdays: the source is from 2024.
  • Juella is 5 km of gravel: 20 slow minutes; not worth it in the midday heat.
  • Purmamarca at sunset: the Cerro de los Siete Colores is in shade (it faces east); its colour is a morning thing. If you go, it is for the Paseo de los Colorados and the fair, not the hill.
  • Last night in the Quebrada: full tank (YPF Tilcara or Humahuaca), cash counted and bags ready to leave Friday 08:30 for Salta (≈ 220 km).
  • Altitude: 2,650 m at the hotel; after four nights you are acclimatised, but the sunny pool dehydrates: drink water.

Day 21 · Fri Dec 11 · Huacalera → down the Quebrada (Tilcara, Maimará, Volcán) → San Salvador de Jujuy → Salta 🛻 Self-drive in the Raptor · Salta · 219 km

🧭 How to get there

LegkmTimeRoadNotes
Hotel Huacalera (RN9 km 1790) → Tilcara17 km15 minRN9 · asfaltoCheckout 10:00 (hotel confirms 10:00 check-out). Leave 09:00 if you want stops; RN9 descends gently along the Río Grande. Tilcara is 1 km off the road across the bridge: only if you need an ATM or pharmacy.
Tilcara → Maimará (mirador Paleta del Pintor)8 km10 minRN9 · asfaltoJust past Maimará on your right, the Paleta del Pintor with the cemetery at its foot: wide shoulder for a 5-minute stop. Best light in the morning.
Maimará → Empalme RN52 (Purmamarca)15 km15 minRN9 · asfaltoNo need to turn into Purmamarca (4 km detour): you already know it. Usual fixed speed camera around Purmamarca/Tumbaya: 60 km/h in the villages.
Empalme RN52 → Volcán19 km20 minRN9 · asfaltoTumbaya, Bárcena and Volcán: the gorge narrows and the green of the yungas begins. Watch for donkeys and goats crossing between Tumbaya and Volcán. Volcán has a craft fair and a roadside fruit market.

💡 Tips

  • El Castillo de San Lorenzo is open to the public Wed–Mon 11:00–20:00: Saturday yes; Tuesday no (irrelevant, you fly out that day).
  • For the peña leave the Ranger at the hotel: taxi/remis both ways (La Casona del Molino is 4.5 km away and closes 04:00; Balderrama 2.5 km).
  • Saturday is peak peña night: book Balderrama by phone or La Vieja Estación online; La Casona del Molino takes no bookings, arrive at 21:00.
  • Ponchos: check prices today at the Mercado Artesanal (10:00–20:30, open Sunday and Monday too) and buy on Monday the 14th if you want to compare with Tienda La Fortuna (Mon 09–13 and 17–21).
  • Museo Güemes tickets and any Quebrada trail fee are paid on site in cash or card; there is no online sale.

💡 Tips

  • Option B (Cachi in the Ranger): NO. It is 157 km each way (OSRM 3 h 01; +20 % for mountain ≈ 3 h 35), the Cuesta del Obispo has ≈ 20 km of consolidated gravel and climbs to 3,348 m at Piedra del Molino (Wikipedia; the rest, Recta del Tin Tin and Chicoana, is paved — not 100 km of gravel, but it makes no difference): 7 h at the wheel for 2 h in Cachi, breaks the ≤ 2 h-from-base rule and the no-altitude rule. If you want to see it, it is option A (tour).
  • Option A: book 48 h ahead (by Friday 11th), free cancellation 24 h before; ask via Viator chat to confirm pick-up at the Sheraton (Uriondo 330). Bring warm clothes (cold at 3,300 m even in December), water, cash for lunch in Cachi and sunscreen; lunch is not included in 394075P2 or 31845P4.
  • Option C (free day): open on Sunday: cable car 09–19, MAAM and Museo Güemes 11–19, Mercado Artesanal 10–20:30, Balcarce fair from 10:00. CLOSED on Sunday: Casa de Hernández/City Museum (Mon–Fri) and Museo Pajcha, which is no longer at 20 de Febrero 831 but at UCASAL (Campo Castañares, Mon–Fri 10–13 and 15–18, free): both move to Monday 14th.
  • CLOCK: today at 16:25 online check-in opens for AR1491 (SLA 16:25 → AEP 18:30 on Tuesday). Do it for all 4 (Néstor, Ana, Carolina and Paula, booking UOTFVV) as soon as it opens; if on the tour, from the phone in the minibus.
  • Sunday midday in Salta many restaurants close: Doña Salta and El Charrúa open 11:30; La Casona del Molino 12:00–15:00. José Balcarce is closed on Sunday.
  • If you take the tour, Sunday dinner is late (back 19:30–20:00): El Charrúa opens 19:30, Doña Salta 20:00; neither needs a booking.

Un solo país, una sola moneda: peso argentino (ARS). Referencias del 22–23 oct 2026: dólar oficial BNA vendedor ARS 1.550 por US$ (dolarapi.com) · 1 US$ = 0,8934 € (BCE, frankfurter.dev). Regla de oro: pagar en pesos con tarjeta argentina (sin DCC); efectivo en pesos para accesos de parques, comunidades, ferias y peajes. Se refresca al versionar.
